items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VII, List of Answers on Topics 33:1
items.html: You already know the division of Bina and Tevuna into two halves, GAR and ZAT, that the GAR is the aspect of Bina before she emanated ZON, when she is only the light of Hassadim. And this is the aspect of AVI Ila'in (Upper Aba ve-Ima). And the ZAT, which is the aspect of Bina after she emanated ZON, when she also has the illumination of Hochma, is called Tevuna, and this is the aspect of Yeshsut. And with this you will understand that AVI Ila'in are not attributed at all to being the Rosh of ZON, for on the contrary, the whole essence of AVI Ila'in is because they are the aspect of Bina before she emanated ZON, and they have only the light of Hassadim, which is not at all of the aspect of ZON, who are only the aspect of Hassadim in the illumination of Hochma. Therefore only the Yeshsut, who are the aspect of the ZAT of AVI, who emanated the ZON of AVI, and who have the illumination of Hochma, which is the whole degree of Zeir Anpin, are always considered in all the Partzufim to be the aspect of the Rosh of ZON. (Page 525, Sub Header “And you shall remember”)
